artboards.title: Original — Inventory (first pass), page 3. The shape you described: a tab, a table, a details panel.
Replacement — Listed. The same shell, the same inspector, the estate as a list. No tab bar.
The one change to an approved board: the masthead, before and after
One camera — the list is the far end of the zoom you already have
One inspector — the quick peek and the editor, reached from the list or from the rack
Free space is inventory — runs, ports and inlets as rows, not gaps
First slice worth building — models and firmware, tied to the staging you asked for

annotations.text:
Read across, then down.

Top row: the original first-pass inventory board (left) beside the replacement (right).

Second row: the only change to an approved board, and why the list is the far end of the existing zoom rather than a place.

Third row: the inspector is one component reached two ways; free space gets rows of its own.

Bottom: the narrow first slice, which is the same question the firmware staging work started answering.

Why the original cannot stand: it breaks three rules the approved page-1 shell was chosen for. (1) A tab bar — Diagram, Inventory, Rack, Findings, Walkthrough, Config — where the spec says there is none. (2) A page change, where the spec says zoom is one continuous camera and never a page change. (3) A second details panel beside the canvas's inspector, so two editors sit over one graph and will drift. The table itself, the first-press-selects second-press-edits rule, the credential mark and the Gaps section are all good, and they are kept.

Sample values throughout: device names, Junos versions, the staged image name, hashes and dates are made up to show the shapes. Counts in a real deployment come from the graph and the catalogue and are never typed.
